name: orderbook
algorithm: Replay a recorded market-data feed through a price-time priority matching engine (limit, market, stop and stop-limit orders, cancels, amends, halts, busts and every refusal), then run the batch statistics over the fills, the depth and the close, and print the dogfood's quiet line: the commands, the fills and the FNV-1a checksum over every fill, bust and refusal and the final book (README.md).

hand.c: every container and the feed reader: a hash table (open addressing, backward-shift deletion, 85 lines), growable ring buffers (51 lines), sorted arrays for the price levels and the volume by price, binary heaps for the stops (41 lines), and a CSV line splitter with its number parsers (125 lines); the slot pool and the live bitset are the task's own structure, as in every cell (README.md, Cells)
hand.rust: a CSV splitter for the feed's unquoted fields: BufRead::read_until a line, from_utf8, split on commas, trim (about 50 lines); every other container is std's, the slot pool and the live bitset being the task's own structure, as in every cell (README.md, Cells)
hand.zig: a CSV splitter for the feed's unquoted fields: takeDelimiter a line, std.mem.splitScalar on commas, std.mem.trim, and a sign-and-digits integer parser (about 50 lines); every other container is std's but the price levels, a sorted std.ArrayList (std has a Treap, no B-tree), the slot pool and the live bitset being the task's own structure, as in every cell (README.md, Cells)
hand.cs: a CSV splitter for the feed's unquoted fields: 64 KiB StreamReader, split on commas, trim ASCII whitespace, refuse quotes (about 50 lines); every other container is .NET BCL's (Dictionary, HashSet, SortedList, PriorityQueue, List), the slot pool and the live bitset being the task's own structure, as in every cell (README.md, Cells)

notes: The Mk side is Dogfoods/orderbook unchanged (D-842). Its --quiet still runs the statistics (src/main/output.mk: Write runs stats.Summarize, the depth and the rejects before its quiet branch and builds the JSON report after it), so every twin does the same work after the replay; only the quiet line reaches the checksum. Each twin, run without --quiet, prints the dogfood's text report but its engine heap line, and matched orderbook.exe byte for byte on 114 feeds at the review fix of item 11.37 (README.md, Checking the twins).

Containers: Mk mem.Pool, coll.Bitset, Map and Set (fixed keys), coll.HeapBTree of coll.HeapDeque levels, coll.PriorityQueue, coll.Deque, coll.BTree; Rust std's HashMap and HashSet (RandomState, SipHash-1-3), BTreeMap levels of VecDeque, BinaryHeap, VecDeque; Go maps, a sorted slice of levels (labelled: Go's std has no ordered map), plain slices as queues, container/heap; Zig AutoArrayHashMapUnmanaged for the churning order index (swapRemove avoids AutoHashMapUnmanaged tombstone buildup) and AutoHashMapUnmanaged for done/volume (Wyhash), a sorted ArrayList of std.Deque levels (labelled), std.PriorityQueue, std.Deque; C hand throughout. The sorted level arrays of C, Zig and Go keep the best level last, so a new or emptied best level moves no other level. Every twin keeps orders in a slot pool with generations swept every 4,096 commands, as the dogfood's mem.Pool is, and a bitset of live arrival numbers: the task's own structure, counted as a facility in no cell (README.md, Cells).

The feed is read a record at a time in every column: Mk csv.Records (RFC 4180) over a 64 KiB fs Reader, Go encoding/csv over a 64 KiB bufio.Reader, the others a hand splitter of unquoted fields over a 64 KiB buffer. The orderfeed kind writes no quote.

Overflow: no feed of the row overflows the engine's arithmetic; the checksum's FNV-1a multiply wraps by definition and is written wrapping in every language (Mk *%, Rust wrapping_mul, Zig *%, C uint64_t, Go uint64).
Single-threaded: MK_CARRIERS=1, so the dogfood's one task per bar of statistics runs on one carrier; the twins sum the bars inline.

The publish size (data.bytes) is provisional, and so is the checksum, which is the output of every column at that size (M9 item 11.37, untimed runs). tools/bench verify -publish-size fixes the size in the quiet window, and the checksum changes with it.
